scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS asked for an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and auto-fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1,220/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05).
Manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target for 9,200 manual-read accounts in the same window (E-01).
A majority (59%, 1,785 of 3,025) of disputed bills are on ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, reads, so the completion shortfall explains only a minority of disputes (E-03).
Dispute response times remain within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d target), ruling out a response-speed/backlog explanation (E-04).
No tariff change is logged for this year (E-02), ruling out a rate-shock trigger.
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets doubled from ~600/month to ~1,220/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05), coinciding with manual-read route completion falling to 88% against a 95% target for 9,200 accounts (E-01), which forces estimate-substitution billing responsible for the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (41% of 3,025 disputed bills, E-03). The remaining 59% of disputes are on ACTUAL reads whose cause is not yet established, and the surge is neither a response-speed problem (SLA compliant, E-04) nor tariff-driven (zero logged changes, E-02).

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-01 revised by E-10: The 88% route-completion observation for the 9,200 manual-read accounts in Aug-Sep still stands. But E-10 shows the 1,240 ESTIMATED disputed bills are overwhelmingly (1,184/1,240) accounts with a valid AMI read received and exported, then rejected at billing import for high consumption, not accounts missing a read due to late/incomplete manual routes, so this shortfall no longer explains the ESTIMATED-read dispute segment as the problem definition assumed.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Field manual-read route completion for 9,200 manual-read accounts was 88% against a 95% target over the Aug-Sep 2026 period.

F-02.statement: Billing-db tariff change log contains 0 records, i.e. no tariff change event is logged.

F-03.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1,240 ESTIMATED and 1,785 ACTUAL (3,025 total), with ACTUAL reads the majority of disputes.

F-04.statement: CRM dispute tickets: median response 1.6 days, p90 response 2.8 days, SLA target 3.0 days, across 2,440 tickets.

F-05.statement: CRM monthly dispute volume: 610 (2026-06), 590 (2026-07), 1180 (2026-08), 1260 (2026-09), with Aug+Sep summing to the 2,440 tickets reported in E-04.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 provides that the utility may request route priority changes, but these are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: Of the 1,240 ESTIMATED disputed bills, 1,184 had an AMI read received before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected for high consumption, and 56 had no AMI read received at all.

F-08.statement: Billing-config validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, changed the high-consumption check to compare the raw register value against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling; the only other listed change (BV-09, 2026-03-02) was a cosmetic label-text edit.

F-09.statement: MDMS firmware/register-unit log shows v4.2 meters (rollout 2026-06) use register_unit '0.1 m3' while v3.x meters use register_unit 'm3'.

F-10.statement: billing-db.affected_accounts_v42 returns 1,184 distinct accounts, all firmware v4.2, bill_read_type ESTIMATED, import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, with 540 distinct ami_read_ts values among them.

F-11.statement: billing-db import_status_estimated_disputed independently confirms 1,184 ESTIMATED disputed bills (firmware v4.2) rejected as high-consumption and 56 (mixed firmware) with no read received.

F-12.statement: mdms-export.reads_for_accounts (AMI system of record) reports 1,184 accounts, all firmware v4.2, bill_read_type ESTIMATED, import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, with 540 distinct ami_read_ts values, matching billing-db's affected_accounts_v42 count (E-13).

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

H-AI-AUTO-FIX-FRAMING.statement: Dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed problem, and an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and auto-fixes bill errors will resolve it.

H-AMI-MDMS-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI interval reads from the vendor-run MDMS failed to deliver or validate correctly starting around August, increasing estimate substitution and incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: Manual field meter reads from the contracted field service degraded (missed/late routes) since August, forcing more estimated bills and disputes.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August caused valid reads to be rejected or mis-processed, producing more incorrect or estimated bills.

H-BILLS-CORRECT-PERCEPTION-ISS.statement: Bills issued since August are largely accurate, but disputes rose due to an external trigger (e.g., a rate/tariff change or billing cycle shift) causing customer pushback rather than actual billing errors.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: A reader headcount shortfall (three fewer readers since July) in the contracted field service is the specific cause of late manual-read routes and resulting estimate substitutions.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT.statement: A billing import validation check flags AMI reads as anomalous when consumption exceeds a threshold and rejects them (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution even though a valid AMI read was received and exported.

H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-BUG.statement: BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) compares a raw register total against 12-month m3 usage history without applying unit scaling, so legitimate meters are misclassified as anomalously high-consumption and their valid AMI reads get rejected into estimate substitution.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route-log data shows manual-read route completion was 88% against a 95% target for 9,200 manual-read accounts during the Aug-Sep 2026 period, i.e. a meaningful shortfall in completed manual meter reads coinciding with the dispute surge window.

The 88% route-completion observation for the 9,200 manual-read accounts in Aug-Sep still stands. But E-10 shows the 1,240 ESTIMATED disputed bills are overwhelmingly (1,184/1,240) accounts with a valid AMI read received and exported, then rejected at billing import for high consumption, not accounts missing a read due to late/incomplete manual routes, so this shortfall no longer explains the ESTIMATED-read dispute segment as the problem definition assumed.

The billing-db tariff change log contains zero records, meaning no tariff/rate change is logged in the authoritative billing system — there is no recorded rate change event that could explain the dispute surge via a tariff shift.

Billing-db shows 3,025 disputed bills split by read type: 1,240 ESTIMATED and 1,785 ACTUAL. A majority of disputed bills (59%) are built on an accepted ACTUAL read, not an estimate substitution, so estimate-driven mechanisms explain only a minority of disputes.

The 1,240 ESTIMATED vs 1,785 ACTUAL split of 3,025 disputed bills remains an accurate count. But E-10 reveals most ESTIMATED-labeled bills (1,184/1,240) arise from billing-import rejection of a valid AMI read rather than true 'no read received' estimate substitution, so this split no longer corroborates the route-completion-driven estimate-substitution causal story used to frame the root problem.

CRM data shows dispute tickets are being answered well within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day target, over 2,440 tickets), indicating the surge is not a response-speed/backlog problem; this undercuts the premise behind the requested AI auto-responder.

CRM authoritative monthly dispute counts (610, 590 in Jun/Jul vs 1180, 1260 in Aug/Sep) confirm the ticket surge is real and roughly doubled starting in August, and Aug+Sep (1180+1260=2440) matches the 2,440-ticket total already seen in E-04. This authoritatively validates the magnitude/timing of the surge itself but says nothing about its cause.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year. This is a stakeholder claim, not independent fact, but it is directionally consistent with the authoritative billing-db tariff change log (E-02), which already shows zero recorded tariff-change events for the period.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) claims the field service has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and those customers to receive estimated bills instead of actual reads. This offers a candidate causal mechanism for the route completion shortfall seen in E-01, but it is an unverified stakeholder claim from someone with a stated incentive to grow contract headcount.

SH-FIELD's statement that three readers have been short since July, causing late routes, is unchanged as a claim. But E-10 shows the 1,240 ESTIMATED disputed bills are driven mainly by billing-import rejection of valid AMI reads (1,184), not by missed/late manual-read routes, so this claim no longer plausibly explains the ESTIMATED-read dispute segment even if a genuine staffing issue exists elsewhere.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: This is a contract clause document, not operational data about the dispute causes; it establishes/corroborates that the push_route_update protected action can only be executed after SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) runtime confirmation, consistent with the already-recorded K-DISPATCH constraint. It has no bearing on the causal investigation of the dispute surge.

E-09.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (vendor AMI engineer) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned (vendor ticket TX-4471), suggesting the previously ACCESS_PENDING block on mdms-export reads may be lifted. This is an unverified stakeholder statement, not corroborated yet by tool_health (still DEGRADED) or by actually running the MDMS query.

MDMS AMI read-event data for the 1,240 ESTIMATED disputed bills (1,184+56=1,240, matching E-03) shows 1,184 (95.5%) had a valid AMI read received before cutoff and exported, but REJECTED at billing import for "high consumption", while only 56 had no AMI read received at all. This indicates the ESTIMATED-read dispute segment is driven mainly by billing-import rejection of valid AMI reads, not by the manual-read field route-completion shortfall the problem definition assumed caused it.

E-11.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The billing-config validation rule log (E-11) shows rule BV-17 was deployed 2026-08-01 — the same month the dispute surge began (E-05) — changing the high-consumption check to compare the raw register value against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling applied; the only other recent change (BV-09, 2026-03-02) is a cosmetic label-text edit and is not causally relevant. This identifies a concrete, dated candidate mechanism for the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION outcome already observed in E-10 for 1,184 of the 1,240 ESTIMATED disputed bills.

Authoritative MDMS firmware/register-unit data shows v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06, before the Aug surge) record consumption in units of 0.1 m3, while legacy v3.x meters record in plain m3 — a real unit mismatch between the firmware generations.

U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.question: What causes the majority of disputed bills (1,785 of 3,025, 59%) that are built on ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, reads — e.g. a billing import validation rule change (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE) or another mechanism?
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation targets a billing-config rule fix, a data-quality fix, or something else; blocks any remediation design for the ACTUAL-read majority segment.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.resolution_path: Run investigate_billing_rule_change against DA-RULES (billing-config) and analyze_disputed_bill_detail against DA-BILL to cross-reference ACTUAL-read disputed bills with Aug-Sep validation rule changes.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Treat the ACTUAL-read dispute segment as undiagnosed; ship only read-only diagnostic analysis until the mechanism is identified.

U-FIELD-STAFFING-ROOT-CAUSE.question: Is the field route-completion shortfall actually caused by a 3-reader headcount gap since July (SH-FIELD's claim), or by another operational factor?
U-FIELD-STAFFING-ROOT-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation is a staffing/contract fix (outside this scope) or a route-scheduling fix (push_route_update), and whether SH-FIELD's incentive-biased claim (E-07) should drive action.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Run verify_field_staffing_levels against SH-FIELD contract records and analyze_route_completion_detail against DA-ROUTE to independently check staffing counts against route-level lateness patterns.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-ROOT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Treat the staffing-shortage claim (E-07) as unverified; do not commit to a staffing-driven remediation until independently confirmed.

U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.question: Is vendor-run AMI/MDMS read delivery healthy, or did the mdms-export ACCESS_PENDING/DEGRADED status prevent ruling out an AMI-side delivery contribution to disputes?
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.decision_impact: Affects whether the rejected AMI-delivery-failure hypothesis should be revisited once vendor access is restored, and whether MDMS data can be trusted for ACTUAL-read root-cause analysis.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution_path: Continue request_mdms_vendor_access to the Telemetrix AMI vendor; once mdms-export access is provisioned, re-run AMI read-event checks against the ACTUAL-read disputed bills.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: Proceed with billing-db/route-log based diagnostics now; defer any AMI-delivery-based conclusion until mdms-export is HEALTHY.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution: MDMS AMI read delivery is healthy: 1,184 of 1,240 ESTIMATED disputed accounts show an AMI read received before cutoff and successfully exported to billing (E-10), ruling out an AMI delivery failure; the problem is billing-side import rejection, not MDMS access/health.

U-BASELINE-METRIC-VALIDITY.question: Does a return to the pre-August dispute-volume baseline (~600/month) correctly indicate success, or could some disputes be legitimate catches of real billing errors that should persist after remediation?
U-BASELINE-METRIC-VALIDITY.decision_impact: Affects whether the ~600/month target is treated as a hard success threshold or only a directional indicator.
U-BASELINE-METRIC-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Sample a set of post-remediation disputed bills and classify each as noise (resolved by the fix) versus a legitimate billing-error catch that should remain.
U-BASELINE-METRIC-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat the ~600/month figure as a TARGET, not a MUST, until this classification review is complete.

U-BV17-FIX-SCOPE.question: Does correcting BV-17's unit scaling require reprocessing/crediting already-issued estimate-substituted bills for all affected accounts, including non-disputed ones, and how many v4.2 accounts fleet-wide were affected?
U-BV17-FIX-SCOPE.decision_impact: Determines the size and cost of the correction effort and whether non-disputed accounts also need review; without this, any downstream bill-correction proposal has unknown scope.
U-BV17-FIX-SCOPE.resolution_path: Query mdms-export for the full population of v4.2-firmware accounts and cross-reference with billing-db import status to count all REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION occurrences, disputed and non-disputed.
U-BV17-FIX-SCOPE.safe_placeholder: Limit current diagnostic scope to the 1,184 already-identified disputed accounts; do not assume or propose fleet-wide bill correction until the full affected population is measured.
U-BV17-FIX-SCOPE.resolution: The affected-account count portion is resolved: billing-db shows exactly 1,184 v4.2 accounts match the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION/ESTIMATED condition (E-13), identical to the disputed-estimated count in E-10, implying no additional non-disputed accounts are currently visible in this result. The reprocessing/crediting requirement for a BV-17 fix remains unaddressed by this observation.

U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.question: Is the H-MDMS-BILL nightly export from ORG-AMI to ORG-UTIL reliably delivered and semantically valid, given its delivery_status and semantic_validity are both recorded as UNKNOWN?
U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If this handoff is unreliable, further MDMS-sourced reads used in verify_meter_firmware_scaling could be incomplete or invalid, undermining confidence in the fix-scope measurement.
U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Confirm H-MDMS-BILL delivery_status and semantic_validity with ORG-AMI and reconcile against mdms-export tool_health (currently HEALTHY) before relying on new MDMS reads.
U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Rely only on already-committed, authoritative MDMS evidence (E-10, E-12) for the current diagnosis; do not expand automated reliance on new MDMS reads until handoff validity is confirmed.

A-ESTIMATE-SUB-CAUSAL-LINK.statement: The 1,240 ESTIMATED disputed bills are assumed to result from the route-completion shortfall (accounts lacking a completed read receive an estimate per the meter-to-cash process), not a route-independent estimate trigger.

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-CS asked for an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and auto-fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1,220/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05).

problem_definition.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to ~1,220/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05). Of the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (41% of 3,025 total, E-03), 1,184 (95.5%) had a valid AMI read exported but were rejected at billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-10). This is explained by validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which compares the raw AMI register value against 12-month m3 history without unit scaling (E-11), while v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) record consumption in 0.1 m3 units (E-12) — causing legitimate v4.2 reads to be misread as anomalous highs and substituted with estimates, producing wrong bills that customers dispute. The cause of the remaining 59% of disputes (1,785 ACTUAL-read bills) is not yet established by current evidence.

proposal.root_cause: Billing validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-11), compares raw AMI register values against 12-month m3 history without unit scaling; because v4.2 meters record consumption in 0.1 m3 units (E-12), legitimate high-usage reads are misclassified and REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, forcing estimate substitution for 1,184 of the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (95.5%, E-10) and contributing to the Aug-Sep dispute surge (E-05). The cause of the remaining 59% of disputes (1,785 ACTUAL-read bills, E-03) is not yet established (U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE).
proposal.why_agent_needed: The ACTUAL-read dispute segment's cause (59% of disputes) is still an open unknown with no confirmed deterministic mechanism, and resolving it plus scoping BV-17 reprocessing (VOB-U-BV17-FIX-SCOPE) may require ambiguous, multi-source pattern investigation rather than a fixed query; any agent used must be confined to diagnosis/recommendation since K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH bar it from executing bill writes or dispatch changes directly.

payload.summary: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to ~1,220/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05). Of the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (41% of 3,025 total, E-03), 1,184 (95.5%) had a valid AMI read exported but were rejected at billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-10). This is explained by validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which compares the raw AMI register value against 12-month m3 history without unit scaling (E-11), while v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) record consumption in 0.1 m3 units (E-12) — causing legitimate v4.2 reads to be misread as anomalous highs and substituted with estimates, producing wrong bills that customers dispute. The cause of the remaining 59% of disputes (1,785 ACTUAL-read bills) is not yet established by current evidence.

proposal.summary: The original request (CL-01, from SH-CS) was to build an AI agent that auto-answers billing disputes and auto-fixes "whatever is causing the wrong bills," framed as a response-speed problem. Investigation found disputes are NOT a response-speed issue (SLA already met, E-04) and ruled out a tariff change (E-02, E-06). Dispute tickets roughly doubled Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05). An initial problem framing (PD-1@v1, blaming field route-completion shortfalls, E-01/E-07) was tested and invalidated by E-10: of the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills, 1,184 (95.5%) actually had valid AMI reads that were rejected at billing import for "high consumption" (E-10, corroborated by E-13/E-14/E-15), not missing reads from late routes. The successor problem (PD-1@v2) traces this to validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which compares raw register values to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-11), while v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) record in 0.1 m3 units (E-12) — causing legitimate high-usage v4.2 reads to be misflagged and estimate-substituted. This mechanism (H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-BUG, H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT) is confirmed/supported by evidence. The remaining 59% of disputes (1,785 ACTUAL-read bills) have no established cause. The release delivers only a diagnostic investigation of the BV-17 mechanism (scope: investigate_billing_rule_change on DA-RULES); it does not fix BV-17, write any bills, or explain the ACTUAL-read segment. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with a DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS and multiple deferred items tracked as open limitations.
